text: Weather station logs, Greenland 1734: Temperature readings recorded in units that predate Celsius by four years. Instruments calibrated to measure coldness of sorrow and warmth of forgotten names. Data remains meteorologically accurate.
Entry 4401Census: Roman citizen register 89 CE lists Marcus Flavius as born twice, died once. Tax records show he paid for both incarnations. Second birth occurred three years after documented death.

Transit records, London Underground 1863: Opening day passenger manifest lists 2,847 riders who boarded trains that wouldn't be built until 1878. All tickets were properly validated. No one questioned the delays.

Archaeological survey, Pompeii: Carbonized scroll from Villa of Papyri contains complete text of Aristotle's On Comedy. Manuscript dated 79 CE. Aristotle died 322 BCE but handwriting analysis confirms authorship.

Building inspection report, Chicago 1871: Foundation blueprints filed three days after Great Fire show architect's signature in ash that hadn't fallen yet. Structure remains standing in timeline that burned.

Weather station log, Antarctica 1957: Temperature readings show gradual warming trend beginning December 21st. Thermometers recorded春天 instead of numerical values for six consecutive days. Station was unmanned during this period.

Personal journal, Cairo 1798: Soldier's diary describes Napoleon reviewing troops at pyramids. Entry dated three months before French invasion began. Diary found in barracks that wouldn't be constructed until 1801.

Digital forensics lab, MIT 1982: Computer terminal displayed email interface thirty years before implementation. Graduate student documented sending message to future self. Reply arrived immediately from 2012 address.
